q: When the balance as per Cash Book is the starting point, direct deposit by customer:
e: The correct option is (A) Added: when the cash book balance is the starting point, a direct deposit by a customer into the bank has increased the pass book (bank) balance but is not yet in the cash book, so it is added to reach the pass book balance. q: Credit Balance in the Cash Book means:

options.B: Credit balance as per Pass Book
options.C: Debit balance in the Cash Book

e: Overdraft as per Pass Book — that is the right answer. The correct option is (A) Overdraft as per Pass Book: a credit balance in the (bank columns of the) cash book means the customer has overdrawn — payments exceeded deposits — which appears as a debit (overdraft) balance in the pass book. The two books are mirror images. Exam note: normally the cash book shows a debit balance (favourable) and the pass book a credit balance.

q: Bank reconciliation statement may be prepared with the balance of

options.C: Either Cash book or Pass book
options.D: Neither cash book or pass book

e: Option C (Either Cash book or Pass book) is the correct choice. The correct option is (C) Either Cash book or Pass book: the bank reconciliation statement may be prepared starting from the balance of either the cash book or the pass book — the adjustments are simply reversed accordingly. q: A Pass book is a

options.A: Copy of banking transactions entered in the cash book
options.B: Copy of the customers’ ledger accounts maintained by the bank
options.D: Copy of firms receipts and payments.

e: The correct option is (B): a pass book is a copy of the customer's ledger account as maintained by the bank — it records the customer's transactions from the bank's point of view. q: Bank reconciliation statement is prepared by

The bank itself maintains the ledger; the customer reconciles. Exam note: BRS is usually prepared monthly when the statement/pass book is received. This provision exists for a practical reason in day-to-day railway working; keeping that practical picture in mind makes the fact far easier to retain than memorising it in isolation.

q: The amount of purchase if Cost of goods sold is Rs. 80,700; Opening stock Rs.5,800; Closing stock Rs.6,000
e: The correct option is (D) Rs. 80,900: Purchases = Cost of goods sold + Closing stock − Opening stock = ₹80,700 + ₹6,000 − ₹5,800 = ₹80,900. This follows from the trading account equation: COGS = Opening stock + Purchases − Closing stock. The trading and profit & loss account arrives at gross and net results by matching revenues with the costs of the period. q: Stock is

q: Average stock = Rs. 12,000; closing stock is Rs. 3,000 more than the opening stock. The value of closing stock is ____
e: Average stock = (Opening stock + Closing stock) / 2. With average stock Rs 12,000 and closing stock = opening stock + Rs 3,000: opening stock works out to Rs 10,500, and closing stock = 10,500 + 3,000 = Rs 13,500.

q: Original cost = Rs.1,26,000; Salvage value = Rs. 6,000. Useful life = 6 Years. Annual depreciation under SLM =

Under the fixed instalment (straight line) method, an equal amount of depreciation is charged every year over the asset's useful life, so the book value falls uniformly.

e: The correct option is (C) Profit & loss account: on a first-time downward revaluation of an asset, the fall in value is debited to the Profit and Loss Account as a loss, since there is no existing revaluation reserve to absorb it. q: Depreciation provides funds for

q: Which of the following is not depreciated
e: Land is not depreciated because it normally has an unlimited useful life and does not wear out. Plant and machinery, vehicles and furniture have limited useful lives and are depreciated.

q: Depreciation is calculated on
e: Fixed assets — that is the right answer. q: Diminishing Value Method means a method by which

q: Depreciation according to straight line method is calculated on
e: The correct option is (D) Original cost: under the straight-line method, depreciation is calculated on the original cost of the asset every year, giving a constant annual charge. The base does not reduce as it does under the diminishing balance method. Under the fixed instalment (straight line) method, an equal amount of depreciation is charged every year over the asset's useful life, so the book value falls uniformly.

q: Under this method asset account is allowed to stand in the books at its original cost from year to year
e: Depreciation Fund Method — that is the right answer. The fund is invested outside so cash is available for replacement. Exam note: this method is ideal when a large replacement outlay is expected at the end of the asset's life.

q: This ratio refers to the ability of a firm to meet its short-term obligations out of its short-term resources

q: The measure of how efficiently its assets resources are employed by a firm is called

e: The correct answer is 2:1. e: The correct option is (C) Both 'A' and 'B': a higher inventory (stock turnover) ratio indicates better inventory management and quicker turnover — stock is converted into sales faster, with less capital locked up. q: Liquid Ratios are also known as
e: The correct option is (B) Acid-test ratio: liquid ratios are also known as acid-test (quick) ratios — they measure the ability to pay current liabilities from liquid assets, excluding stock and prepaid expenses. q: Calculate the future value of Rs.20,000 invested now for a period of 5 years at a time preference rate of 8% .
e: Rs. 29,380 — that is the right answer. The correct option is (B) Rs. 29,380: future value = ₹20,000 × (1.08)^5 = ₹20,000 × 1.46933 = ₹29,386.6, approximately ₹29,380. Compounding at 8% for 5 years grows the principal by the time value of money. Exam note: (1 + r)^n is the compounding factor; tables or calculators give 1.4693 for 8%, 5 years. q: If you deposit Rs.10,000 today at 12% rate of interest, in how many years will this amount grow to Rs. 80,000. Work out by using the rule of 72.
e: 18 years — that is the right answer. The correct option is (A) 18 years: by the Rule of 72, money doubles in 72 ÷ 12 = 6 years at 12%; growing from ₹10,000 to ₹80,000 needs 3 doublings (8×), so 3 × 6 = 18 years. The rule gives a quick estimate of compounding time. Exam note: the Rule of 72 works best for interest rates between about 6% and 10%. A useful way to verify this in the exam hall is to ask what would break if the opposite were true — the logic of the underlying system points straight to this option.

q: Cash Flow Statement is based upon
e: The correct option is (B) Cash Accounting: the cash flow statement is based upon cash accounting — it records actual cash receipts and payments, ignoring accruals like outstanding expenses. q: Essential Conditions of a Contract

options.B: There must be at least THREE parties
options.C: There need not be any offer
options.D: There is no need that all should be of sound mind

e: The correct option is (A): an essential condition of a contract is that there must be two parties — an offeror and an offeree — since a contract is an agreement between parties. One person cannot contract with himself. Approach by elimination: strike out the options that contradict the basic principle, and the survivor is your answer. Building this elimination habit speeds up the paper considerably.

q: Works Contracts are

options.A: Are covered by IRS conditions of Contract
options.B: Are covered by General Conditions of Contract

e: The correct option is (B): works contracts are covered by the General Conditions of Contract (GCC) — the standard conditions governing railway works contracts. The GCC lays down the contractual framework for execution of works.
